title: SwarmKit Skill
description: A discrete capability an agent can exercise. See design §6 and design/details/skill-schema-v1.md.

inputs.description: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) defining the skill's input shape.

outputs.description: JSON Schema defining the skill's output shape. Passed to providers for structured generation (Tier 0) and used for deterministic validation (Tier 1). See design/details/structured-output-governance.md.

allOf.$comment: Decision skills must emit a human-readable reasoning string so audits and reviews have a rationale alongside the verdict. See design/details/skill-schema-v1.md §'Decision-category output contract'.

iam_scope.description: namespace:action — e.g. repo:read, github:write, skills:activate, mcp_servers:*

oneOf.$comment: Invoke a command from a workspace `command_packs` entry. Governed like an mcp_tool: the pack supplies the permission tier, this skill's `iam.required_scopes` supplies the authorization.

Another agent as a skill (design/details/a2a-interop.md). Exactly one of `topology` (a topology in this workspace, run in-process as a child job) or `card_url` (a remote A2A agent's card; the task API is the transport). The tool takes {input, context?}; when the other agent asks a question and `on_unanswerable` is `agent`, it returns {status: input_required, task_id, question} and is called again with {task_id, answer}. There is no server or pack to inherit a tier from, so `permission` and `effects` sit here.

topology.description: A topology in this workspace. Runs as a child job of the caller's run (same correlation, parent_job_id set); no network.

card_url.description: A remote agent's Agent Card URL (usually .../.well-known/agent-card.json). The card's `url` is where the task API is called.

skill_id.description: Remote only: which of the card's skills this skill invokes (sent as message.metadata.skill). Omitted: the card's first skill.

credentials_ref.description: Remote only: a workspace `credentials` entry, resolved by the credential service and sent as a bearer token.

timeout_s.description: How long to wait for the other agent's task to finish before the call fails.

on_unanswerable.description: What happens when the other agent asks a question — the same words a harness adapter uses for a mid-run request. relay: a person answers through the review queue (bounded wait, never hangs). abort: the call fails with the question as the reason. agent: the question is the tool result and the calling agent answers it, bounded by max_agent_answers and audited; past the budget it relays. A human gate on the other side is never the agent's to resolve, whatever this says.

max_agent_answers.description: Under `agent`: how many questions the calling agent may answer on one task before the next one is relayed to a person.

permission.description: Governance tier for the call, as an MCP server's `permission` is for its tools.

effects.description: What calling this agent does to the world. Under `readonly`, only `read` is allowed — `unknown` is denied, fail-closed, as for MCP tools.

audit.description: Controls what gets logged when this skill executes. Per-skill privacy/compliance control.

log_inputs.description: How much of the skill's input to log. Default varies by category: decision=full, capability=summary.

log_outputs.description: How much of the skill's output to log.

redact.description: JSON paths to redact from logged inputs/outputs (e.g. '$.password', '$.api_key').

requires_runtime.$comment: The minimum swarmkit-runtime this skill needs. A catalogue skill outgrows the runtime that installed it: `command` backing needs >=1.197.0, `requires:` ordering >=1.193.0, declared `effects` under a readonly MCP server >=1.199.0. Without a floor it resolves cleanly into an older workspace and fails at run time naming nothing useful — the swarmkit-webui failure exactly. Checked at workspace load; absent means no constraint.
